design.text: Phase 3, randomized (1:1), active-controlled (palivizumab) study conducted in two parts: Part 1 is double-blind and Part 2 is open-label; primary endpoint was safety, with efficacy and PK as secondary endpoints

citations.quote: Trial MK-1654-007 is an ongoing Phase 3, partially blinded, randomized, active-controlled, multisite study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of clesrovimab versus palivizumab and the pharmacokinetics of clesrovimab in infants who are at increased risk for severe RSV disease, born during or entering their first RSV season (RSV Season 1), and recommended to receive palivizumab. Part 1 of the trial (Day 1 to Day 60 visit in RSV Season 1) is double-blind, and Part 2 (Day 60 visit through trial completion) is open-label. The primary objective/endpoint for Trial MK-1654-007 is evaluation of safety; efficacy and pharmacokinetics are assessed as secondary endpoints.

indication.text: Prevention of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) lower respiratory tract disease in neonates and infants who are born during or entering their first RSV season

citations.quote: ENFLONSIA is indicated for the prevention of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) lower respiratory tract disease in neonates and infants who are born during or entering their first RSV season.

target_moa.text: A monoclonal antibody that preferentially binds the prefusion conformation of the RSV fusion (F) protein at antigenic Site IV, locking the protein in its prefusion state and preventing membrane fusion and viral entry

citations.quote: Clesrovimab is a recombinant human immunoglobulin G1 kappa (IgG1κ) monoclonal antibody (mAb) that preferentially binds the prefusion conformation of the RSV fusion (F) protein.
RB-1 binds to antigenic Site IV, which likely locks the protein in its prefusion state and prevents the irreversible conformational change to the more stable postfusion conformation.
Clesrovimab-cfor is a fully human immunoglobulin G1 kappa (IgG1κ) monoclonal antibody produced in recombinant Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells.

key_safety.text: Generally well tolerated; most common adverse reactions were injection-site erythema (3.7%), injection-site swelling (2.7%) and rash (2.3%); key concerns are potential serious hypersensitivity (anaphylaxis) and serious skin reactions

requirement.text: 4841-2 Conduct a surveillance study of current and emerging respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) variants from global locations, with F protein sequencing and identification of clesrovimab binding site substitutions and their frequency.

citations.quote: 4841-2 Conduct a surveillance study of current and emerging respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) variants from global locations, with F protein sequencing and identification of clesrovimab binding site substitutions and their frequency. These surveillance activities should include active collection and characterization of RSV samples from global regions (i.e., North America [US/Canada], Europe, rest of the world) and will target at least 100 samples from each region when fully operational, as well as periodic analysis of sequences from public databases (i.e., GISAID, NCBI, GenBank). The surveillance study should also determine the cell culture neutralization activity of clesrovimab against those RSV clesrovimab binding epitope variants carrying substitutions (VAF >10%) and with unknown impact on clesrovimab susceptibility that are capable of growing in cell culture. Phenotypic characterization will include RSV variants whose prevalence is \ge 5\% within an RSV season (or over two consecutive years in public databases) and/or \ge 3-fold increase above 1% from the previous season across all sequenced samples and from all sites within a global region. RSV variants of interest for phenotypic testing will include those carrying substitutions of unknown impact on clesrovimab susceptibility, detected in Site IV, adjacent to the clesrovimab binding epitope (within \le 5 Å distance), or outside Site IV at highly conserved positions (\ge 99\% in GenBank).
